title: The Atmosphere: Composition, Layers, and the Heat Budget

questions.question: The most abundant gas in dry air is:
questions.rationale: Nitrogen makes up 78.08% of dry air, oxygen 20.95%, argon 0.93%, and carbon dioxide only about 0.04%.

questions.question: Almost all weather — clouds, rain, and storms — happens in the:
questions.rationale: The troposphere holds the bulk of the atmosphere's mass and nearly all its water vapour and weather activity.

questions.question: Temperature in the troposphere falls with height at about:
questions.rationale: The normal lapse rate is roughly 6.5°C per kilometre — the reason hill stations are cooler than the plains below.

questions.question: The ozone layer, which shields life from ultraviolet radiation, lies in the:
questions.rationale: Ozone concentrates at 20–25 km in the stratosphere; airliners also cruise near the base of this layer.

questions.question: Meteors burn up as 'shooting stars' in which layer?
questions.rationale: The mesosphere is cold and thin enough that incoming meteors are vaporised before reaching the ground.

questions.question: Radio waves are reflected back to Earth's surface by the:
questions.rationale: The ionised thermosphere (ionosphere) reflects radio waves and also hosts the auroras.

questions.question: Earth is farthest from the Sun (aphelion) in early July at about:
questions.rationale: At perihelion (around 3 January) Earth is about 147 million km from the Sun; at aphelion (around 4 July) it is about 152 million km.

questions.question: In the Earth's heat budget, about how many of every 100 units of insolation are absorbed by the land and ocean surface?
questions.rationale: About 51 units are absorbed by the surface, 19 by the atmosphere, and 30 (the albedo) are reflected and scattered back to space.

questions.question: Albedo, which averages about 30% for the planet, refers to:
options: The rate of temperature fall with height
The fraction of radiation reflected back to space
The share of nitrogen in air
questions.rationale: Albedo is the reflected fraction of incoming radiation; clouds and snow raise it while dark forests and oceans lower it.

questions.question: The atmosphere is heated chiefly by:
options: Direct absorption of sunlight in the thermosphere
Long-wave radiation from the warmed surface below
questions.rationale: Sunlight passes through the air largely unabsorbed, warms the surface, and the surface then heats the air from below by conduction, convection, and long-wave radiation.
